# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration cand_0001 (1/3), empty seed. Baseline val 0.450 (18/40). Every one of the 22 failing traces was diagnosed against its `*_golden.xlsx` answer cells (init value / golden value / golden formula dump). The grader uses `data_only=True` with no recalc. No infra faults were found: every rollout had `error: None`.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula string written instead of computed value | 37378, 46897, 6698, 7902, 8942, 55049, 53383, 9569, 55979, 37456, 54144, 53647, 56563 (~13) | User says "formula/VBA". The agent writes `=...`, which reads back as None (or as error text for TEXTSPLIT/AGGREGATE) under data_only with no recalc. The goldens are literals. | KNOWLEDGE (of grading) + BEHAVIORAL | CONTRACT in prompt.md + task_template field description |
| 2 | B. Semantics/layout misread; rule not reconciled with pre-filled examples | 39046, 43436, 48527, 51-12, 227-40, 50768, 267-18 (59196 unclear) | Literal reading of a loose question. Ignores example rows, hint markers, matrix labels, header-encoded params and fills. Global value instead of per-row. Header row of a mirrored block omitted. | BEHAVIORAL | Ordered PROCEDURE (inspect → derive rule → check vs examples) |
| 3 | C. Final write via pandas `to_excel` / ExcelWriter | 80-42, 227-40, 39046, 48527, 50768, 55049 (xlsxwriter missing) | Rewrites the sheet, drops other sheets, shifts rows through header handling | KNOWLEDGE | Procedure step 4 + practical notes |
| 4 | D. No verification; output_path retyped | 51-12 (typo `_0-`), most failing traces (never reload output) | The built-in template said "once that file exists, you are done", so the agent never reloads its output | BEHAVIORAL | task_template interaction contract + procedure step 5/6 |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CONTRACT + KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md "How your result is judged" | Explains why formulas score zero (no cached value) and treats "formula/VBA/how can I" as "produce the values". Covers every formula task, not specific functions. | Yes. All 18 passing tasks already write literals. |
| A | CONTRACT | task_template.md instruction field + step 2 | Restates "literal values, never formula strings" in the user message the agent reads first | Same as above |
| A | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md types bullet | Real int/float/str/datetime, no "#N/A" strings, follow the examples for not-found cases | Passing tasks already use these types |
| B | PROCEDURE | prompt.md steps 1–3 | Inspect target region/examples/fills, derive the rule from the sheet, check that it reproduces the examples, evaluate per row | Adds inspection only. Passing tasks either have no examples or already match them. |
| C | KNOWLEDGE/STRUCTURE | prompt.md step 4 + notes | openpyxl load → set target cells → save to output_path. Explains why `to_excel` damages layout. Notes that xlsxwriter is absent. | Phrased as a reasoned preference. Passing pandas users (e.g. 142-12) would get the same values via openpyxl. |
| B | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md step 4 | Fill the whole answer range. Include the header row when the block starts at a header. Leave unused trailing cells empty. | Only applies when the range starts at a header row |
| D | PROCEDURE/CONTRACT | task_template.md steps 1–3 + prompt.md steps 5–6 | Reload with data_only and print the answer range, fix if wrong, then finish with a no-code reply. This matches the adapter's real loop: a no-code reply after the file exists ends the run, and up to 3 verify rounds are allowed. | Passing tasks that end with prose already behave this way |
| D | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md practical notes | Copy the exact output_path string; its dir exists | — |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- A (8942): wrote `=SUMPRODUCT(...)` to Overview!B5, which reads back None. The contract says to compute the monthly sum in Python and write a number. The verify step would then print B5=None for a formula and flag it.
- A (46897, 6698, 7902, 55049): the same pattern of COUNTIF/INDEX, COUNTIFS, IF/VLOOKUP/SUMIFS and SUMPRODUCT formula strings. Each trace already has the logic, so computing it in pandas/openpyxl is direct.
- A (54144 TEXTSPLIT, 56563 AGGREGATE): error-text readback is covered by "never write error text" and "no formula".
- B (39046): pre-filled F2:F4 show per-row counts 2,2,0. Step 2 ("reproduce every example; per row, not global") targets exactly the global-count mistake.
- B (48527): pre-filled examples contradicted the literal reading. Step 2 forces reconciliation.
- B (43436): the month is in the header text, and counts are per department. Step 2 names "header text that encodes a parameter".
- B (267-18): fill detection. Step 3 says to print fgColor for the candidate rows before choosing.
- B (227-40): header row omitted from a dedup block. Step 4's header-row rule plus the "leave trailing cells empty" rule.
- C (80-42, 50768): `to_excel` shifted or overwrote layout. Step 4 says openpyxl targeted write.
- D (51-12): output_path was retyped with `_0-`, giving FileNotFoundError. The note says to copy the exact string. Step 2 of the procedure (hint markers 1–4 in row 2) targets its count.
- Template check: parsed the template with string.Formatter after stripping the comment. It has all 6 required placeholders plus max_turns and no unknown ones, and `.format()` succeeds. prompt.md is not `.format`-ed (adapter line 1378), so braces there are safe. It contains none anyway.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none. I worked serially, because the system instructions say not to use Agent/Workflow unless the user asks.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md: this is the first iteration (empty seed), so there was no prior work. rejected.jsonl/history.jsonl are empty.
- Blast radius: prompt.md and task_template.md are global text. Risk to passing tasks is low because every rule codifies what the passing traces already do (literal values, targeted write, prose finish). The main residual risk is that a longer inspection procedure uses more rounds. This is bounded: the adapter has 30 rounds and only counts verify rounds after a write.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The "formulas read back empty, so write computed literals" contract. It is the single highest-leverage fact for this grader (hard_no_recalc).
- The verify-then-no-code-finish loop, which matches the adapter's VERIFY_TURNS mechanics.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- 59196: the agent computed values but the range read empty. The cause (row offset vs. sheet choice) is unverified, so I added no specific rule. The generic verify step may catch it.
- No task-specific rules (e.g. risk-matrix orientation for 50768), to avoid overfitting. These are covered generically by "labels on a matrix" in step 2.
- No worked example this iteration. I kept the prompt short for the first measurement. A compact example of formula request → computed literal is a candidate lever for iteration 2 if cluster A persists.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
